# Deploy DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GPU Cloud for 1M-Context Inference

...

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 552B backbone parameters, 8B active per prompt token and 16B per generated token, and a 1,048,576-token context.
- Its global KV cache is 890 bytes per token, so a full one-million-token prompt needs under 1 GB of global KV.
- A DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash deployment fits on one 8x NVIDIA H100 machine once the Engram tables and their scales, about 189 GiB, move to pinned host memory, leaving about 36 GiB of resident weights on each card.
- vLLM 0.31.0 serves it with tensor parallel 8, a 4,096-token batch budget and 0.92 memory utilisation, the NVIDIA H100 configuration from the vLLM recipe.
- The endpoint serves thinking with a 1 to 100 effort setting, OpenAI-format tool calls and image input, and Claude Code can drive it directly.
- The whole deployment runs on one machine at $20.80 per hour on demand, or from $14.56 per hour reserved, billed per minute.

...

The 8x NVIDIA H100-80G-PCIe-NVLink flavour bridges each card to one neighbour with NVLink, which Hyperstack rates at 600 GB/s bidirectional on its NVIDIA H100 PCIe page, and reaches the other six cards over PCIe Gen5 through the host bridge. Tensor parallel 8 spans all eight cards, so every all-reduce uses both kinds of link. Our guide to distributed inference with vLLM explains how tensor parallelism splits each layer across GPUs.

...

## DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Deployment Cost

A DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash deployment on one machine comes down to one hourly GPU rate. Hyperstack lists NVIDIA H100 NVLink at $2.60 per GPU hour on demand and from $1.82 per GPU hour reserved on its GPU pricing page, and this machine carries eight cards. The public IP the endpoint needs is listed separately on the same page, at $0.00672043 per hour. Billing runs per minute, as the billing policies set out, and starts once the machine is ACTIVE, as the getting started guide notes.

What a month of runtime costs

Drag the slider to the hours the machine runs. Billing is per minute, so a partial hour costs only the minutes used.

Chart: cost of the 8x NVIDIA H100 machine for a chosen number of hours. At 730 hours, on demand at $20.80 per hour is $15,184.00 and reserved from $14.56 per hour is $10,628.80.

On-demand and reserved rates for eight NVIDIA H100 NVLink GPUs, from the pricing page.

### Three Levers on the Bill

What moves the cost, and how

One lever is a commitment, one is a per-request setting and one is a habit.

| Lever | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Reserved pricing | From $1.82 against $2.60 per GPU hour, 30 per cent lower, for an endpoint that runs continuously. |
| Reasoning effort | Sets how many tokens each answer spends, and so the cost of each answer on a machine billed by the hour. DeepSeek finds most of the maximum accuracy between 60 and 80, at under half the tokens of 100. |
| Hibernation between sessions | This flavour supports hibernation, which bills only the root disk while the machine is paused. Keep a copy of the checkpoint on a shared storage volume, because `/ephemeral` does not persist through it. Shared storage is listed at $0.000096774 per GB per hour, about $0.05 per hour for the 510 GB checkpoint. |

Hibernation support and billing from the flavour reference; storage behaviour from the ephemeral storage guide; the shared storage rate from the GPU pricing page.

# Dedicated Inference: Deploy a Private Model Endpoint on Hyperstack

TABLE OF CONTENTS

### Key Takeaways

- Hyperstack Dedicated Inference puts one open-weight model on GPUs reserved for your organisation, behind a private, API key-protected HTTPS endpoint.
- The Deploy AI wizard sizes the GPU to the model, its context and its concurrency, checks stock, creates the machine and installs vLLM in one pass.
- Sizing is arithmetic: model weights plus KV cache plus runtime overhead, checked against 90 per cent of the card’s advertised VRAM.
- Every endpoint speaks the OpenAI-compatible chat completions API, so existing SDKs and client libraries work unchanged; agentic tool calling works too, described in the prompt rather than the OpenAI tools parameter, since vLLM only turns that parameter on when its server is launched with matching tool-call flags.
- The endpoint provisions on demand and bills per minute at the flavour’s hourly rate, for as long as the machine runs.

Hyperstack Dedicated Inference puts a single open-weight model on GPUs reserved for your organisation, reachable at an HTTPS endpoint that only its own API key can call.

...

The panel also reports what the configuration serves, which can exceed what you asked for, as it does here. The machine behind it carries 28 vCPUs and 58 GB of RAM, and the quoted rate was $0.5067 an hour, close to $370 a month if left running continuously.

...

Shown alongside the summary, on the same screen.

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Rate | $0.5067 / hour |
| If always on | ≈ $370 / month |
| Deploys and builds | Free |

## Sizing and Cost in Practice

A dedicated endpoint bills per minute at the hourly rate of the flavour it runs on, for as long as the machine is running, regardless of how many requests it serves. The Deploy AI wizard provisions on demand only; Reserved and Spot are not options inside the wizard itself.

Rates follow the standard virtual machine rates in the Pricebook, the same rates that apply to any Hyperstack virtual machine.

What an always-on endpoint costs, on demand

Published on-demand hourly rates multiplied by 730 hours, the same monthly convention the wizard’s own “always-on” estimate uses.

Chart: estimated monthly cost if run continuously on demand, $365 for the NVIDIA RTX A6000 and $730 for the NVIDIA L40.

Hourly rates from the Hyperstack GPU pricing page.

| GPU | VRAM | Memory bandwidth | On demand |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA RTX A6000 | 48 GB GDDR6 | 768 GB/s | $0.50/hr |
| NVIDIA L40 | 48 GB GDDR6 | 864 GB/s | $1.00/hr |

Both cards carry the same 48 GB of VRAM, so the choice between them for a model this size is about throughput rather than fit.

The NVIDIA L40’s higher memory bandwidth and newer Ada Lovelace core suit a busier endpoint, while the NVIDIA RTX A6000 on the Cost profile is the cheaper way to hold a model of this size on a private endpoint.

The sizing profile is the lever that matters most. Cost picks the cheapest fit, Fast the quickest GPU class, Experiment the fewest GPUs at a shorter context, all before any pricing decision is made.

...

### How is a dedicated endpoint priced?

At an hourly rate, provisioned on demand and billed per minute regardless of traffic. A single NVIDIA RTX A6000 is $0.50/hour.

# How to Choose a Dedicated GPU Cloud Provider

TABLE OF CONTENTS

### Key Takeaways

- The word "dedicated" covers everything from reserved slices of a shared pool to physically isolated clusters, so every evaluation should start by making each provider state which layers are shared with other customers.
- Isolation matters most at the GPU fabric, storage and compute layers, where neighbouring workloads cause both benchmark variance and slow InfoSec reviews.
- An SLA is only as credible as the standby hardware and support model behind it, and the consumption model decides how much of the stack your own team has to run.
- Hyperstack's Dedicated Cloud delivers single-tenant NVIDIA GPU clusters as GPU VMs through the same portal and API as its public-cloud regions, with the highest SLA of the four Secure Private Cloud tiers and a fixed monthly cost.

...

The difficulty is that almost every GPU cloud now calls some part of its offering dedicated, and the term means very different things from one provider to the next. These are usually commitments of a year or more, so an evaluation built on headline GPU counts and hourly rates can lock a team into infrastructure that solves the wrong problem. The questions below separate dedicated infrastructure from renamed shared capacity.

...

## 7. Price the Contract on Utilisation, Not on Hourly Rate

On a fixed contract of a year or longer, the hourly equivalent rate matters far less than the proportion of capacity your organisation actually uses, because idle GPUs cost the same as busy ones. Ask whether you can divide the cluster between departments, place workloads dynamically and repurpose idle capacity for research or spot-style jobs, since these capabilities turn one large commitment into a shared internal resource with a predictable cost per useful GPU-hour.

Dedicated builds are designed for sustained, large-scale demand, so the honest first question is whether your usage justifies one yet. Teams running short experiments or dealing with highly variable demand are often better served by on-demand GPU VMs until their usage pattern supports a long-term commitment.

...

## Why Choose Hyperstack Dedicated Cloud

We offer Dedicated Cloud as one of the deployment models within our Secure Private Cloud, which is dedicated, single-tenant GPU infrastructure with zero oversubscription on contracts of 12 months or longer. With Dedicated Cloud, we deploy Hyperstack and AI Studio directly onto your own cluster and run almost the entire stack for you, which gives you:

· Self-service access to your dedicated NVIDIA GPUs as GPU VMs through the same portal and API used for our public-cloud regions.

· The highest SLA of our Secure Private Cloud deployment models, backed by hot, warm and cold standby hardware.

· Performance that is virtualised, not compromised, with GPUs running at 100% of bare-metal performance inside our GPU VMs and network interface cards passed through using SIOV for full line rate.

· A fixed monthly cost with the flexibility to split capacity across departments and repurpose idle GPUs for spot or R&D use.

· A staffed 24/7/365 help desk where our engineers action hot-node swaps directly.

...

If you are evaluating dedicated GPU infrastructure for training or inference at scale, speak to the Hyperstack team about how Dedicated Cloud would be sized around your workloads.
